findings.body:
If `filter` contains shell metacharacters (e.g. `lanczos; rm -rf /tmp`), the command executes arbitrary attacker-controlled code. The previous `execFile` form with an argv array prevented this; the new `exec` form with direct interpolation does not.

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

summary: The PR replaces the safe `execFile` argv form with `exec` and interpolates an untrusted `filter` parameter directly into the shell command. This introduces a command-injection vulnerability. The change is confined to a single 8-line file; no other call sites or callers exist in the repository.

verification.reason: The head code interpolates the unescaped `filter` parameter into `exec(\`... -filter ${filter} ...\`)`, so shell metacharacters run as arbitrary commands. Base used `execFile` with an argv array and no `filter`, so this is a real critical shell-injection regression.
